hero.subtitle: Authorization Code Exchange for web and mobile — Discord application setup, API reference, and frontend examples.

overview.title: Overview
overview.description: Discord login is optional and controlled by DISCORD_AUTH_ENABLED. When disabled, Discord endpoints return 503 Service Unavailable. JWTs are never placed in the redirect URL; the API issues a one-time exchangeCode (Redis, 60 seconds). The same POST /auth/exchange endpoint is shared with other social providers.
items: Profile fetched via GET https://discord.com/api/users/@me after token exchange
Scopes identify and email for profile and email
Same token response shape as POST /auth/login

console.title: Discord Applications
console.description: Create an application under Discord Developer Portal → Applications, open OAuth2, and set the Redirect URI to match DISCORD_CALLBACK_URL. Enable the identify and email scopes.
steps: Create a new application (or select an existing one)
Enable the identify and email scopes
Copy Client ID and Client Secret into your .env
Ensure DISCORD_CALLBACK_URL matches the Redirect URI registered in Discord

env.title: Environment variables
env.description: Loaded from .env via src/config/discord-oauth.config.ts (namespace discordOAuth on ConfigService). See .env.example.

roles.title: Default roles for new Discord users
roles.description: New Discord users receive roles: [] by default (same as password register). Set DISCORD_OAUTH_DEFAULT_ROLES in .env to a comma-separated list of Role values (e.g. user or user,manager). Existing users linked by email keep their current roles.

flow.title: Sequence
items: User consents on Discord; browser hits GET /api/v1/auth/discord/callback
API calls GET https://discord.com/api/users/@me, upserts user, stores exchangeCode in Redis, redirects to redirect?code=...
Client POSTs { code } to /api/v1/auth/exchange and receives JWTs

start.title: 1. Start OAuth
start.description: Opens Discord consent at https://discord.com/api/oauth2/authorize. Query redirect must match a prefix in DISCORD_REDIRECT_ALLOWLIST (or omit to use the first allowlist entry). Scopes: identify email.

callback.title: 2. Callback
callback.description: Handled by the API. Token exchange uses https://discord.com/api/oauth2/token. Redirects to your app with ?code= (or &code= if the URL already has a query).

exchange.title: 3. Exchange code
exchange.description: Public endpoint shared with other social providers. Consumes the code (single use) and returns the same shape as login.

web.title: Frontend — Web (SPA)
web.description: Typical flow: button starts OAuth in the same window (or popup); a callback route on your frontend origin reads code from the query string and calls exchange.
notes: Add your frontend callback URL to DISCORD_REDIRECT_ALLOWLIST (e.g. http://localhost:5173/auth/callback)
DISCORD_CALLBACK_URL must point at the Nest API, not the SPA
Store accessToken / refreshToken securely (memory + httpOnly cookie patterns as you prefer)

mobile.title: Frontend — Mobile (deep link)
mobile.description: Use a custom scheme (or universal link) in the allowlist. After Discord, the API redirects to myapp://success?code=.... The app opens, parses the code, and calls exchange.
notes: Register the scheme in the OS / Expo app.json
Exchange over HTTPS against your API base URL

security.title: Security notes
items: Redirect URLs must match DISCORD_REDIRECT_ALLOWLIST prefixes
Exchange codes are single-use and expire in 60 seconds (Redis)
Existing local users are linked by verified Discord email (discordId set; roles unchanged)
Discord-only users have password null — password login / change-password will fail until a password is set
Email is required from discord.com/api/users/@me; login fails if Discord does not return an email (scopes identify and email)

userModel.title: User model
userModel.description: Postgres entity / interface fields used by Discord login:
items: discordId — unique nullable Discord user snowflake (id from /users/@me)
isActive — set true for new Discord users
